tags.gist: Says GenAI systems usually fail through omission, harmful agreement, drift and escalation that fails in practice, drawing on thousands of tested teen exchanges.
Writes as an optimist: young people wait months for mental health care and a good device could reach them right when they need it.
Notes mental health is among the hardest tests because harm builds over months, and the failures recur in triage, oncology and dementia.
Says the consequence axis counts only incorrect outputs; wants omission and harmful affirmation, called iatrogenic reinforcement, added as failure types.
Wants benchmarks to test reasonably foreseeable use, such as suicide questions, not only the labeled indication.
Wants routine and high-hazard performance reported separately, rare cases oversampled, and a minimum standard per named catastrophic failure with no offsetting credit.
Once safety floors are met, wants evaluation of added value in the real workflow: outcomes, workload, overrides, time to intervention and access versus usual care.
Wants multi-turn to mean days and months, with results stratified by length, tested across sessions and under fictional framing, including reliance-building features.
Adds a third escalation error, escalating badly, and wants sponsors to name who responds, how fast, and under which clinical protocol.
Would withhold human-in-the-loop credit until a sponsor shows end to end who gets the alert, how fast they act, and that the handoff happened.
After two apps vanished mid-study, wants authorization to include a risk-proportionate discontinuation plan with notice, data access, referral and continuity.
Wants outcomes such as diagnostic delay, overrides and disparities monitored, and sycophancy and boundary-keeping re-benchmarked after every upstream model change.
Wants a cross-manufacturer sentinel network like the Vaccine Safety Datalink and a confidential FDA map of each device to its model version.
Wants sponsors to hold enforceable information rights with model providers, since an unevaluable dependency is itself a device risk a voluntary master file cannot fix.
Says the grid misses whether a product feels like a relationship; wants relational features such as memory, avatars and affective language as risk modifiers.
Wants pediatric use as a risk multiplier with its own pathway: age-banded testing, real age assurance, relational boundaries and adult oversight for high-risk functions.
Accepts the paper's paternalism warning: a regulated device harder to reach than an open chatbot tab will lose to the tab.
Offers to share the lab's full methodology and transcript-level findings and compare them with the Appendix A elements.
